records.real_world_identity_notes: RaceRoom's BMW M4 GT3 DTM label identifies the BMW M4 GT3 customer-racing car used in the 2024 DTM season; DTM is the series context, not a separate real-car model. BMW's M4 GT3 is based on the 2021 M4 Competition Coupe and entered customer competition for the 2022 season. The exact RaceRoom game/content build is unknown. BMW establishes a six-speed sequential Xtrac transmission and an electro-hydraulic clutch operated by steering-wheel paddles with partially automated start-up and stall prevention. The reviewed manufacturer material does not establish the exact running-shift technique, automatic cut/blip behavior, or database-level wheel-rim geometry, so those fields remain unknown in this research proposal.

records.specification_basis: BMW describes the M4 GT3's Xtrac transaxle as a six-speed sequential gearbox and repeats the six-speed specification in the technical comparison. BMW explicitly describes the transmission as a straight-toothed six-speed sequential gearbox. The proposal uses the repository vocabulary value sequential and does not silently reclassify straight-toothed as dogbox. BMW establishes a sequential gearbox and a steering-wheel paddle interface for the M4 GT3's electro-hydraulic clutch and driver controls. This supports the existing curated sequential-paddles category, while the source does not separately document every paddle's function. BMW explicitly calls the M4 GT3 gearbox sequential.
